record.original_question: Let (M 3 , F ) be a closed 3-dimensional reversible Finsler manifold of positive flag curvature and N be a closed totally geodesic 2-dimensional submanifold.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^3, F)$ be a closed 3-dimensional reversible Finsler manifold of positive flag curvature, and let $N \subset M^3$ be a closed totally geodesic 2-dimensional submanifold. (Recall that a Finsler metric $F$ is reversible if $F(x,-v) = F(x,v)$ for every tangent vector; the flag curvature is the Finsler analogue of sectional curvature; and $N$ is totally geodesic if every $F$-geodesic of $M$ that is tangent to $N$ at one point stays in $N$.)

Prove or disprove: every closed geodesic of $(M^3, F)$ either intersects $N$ or lies entirely in $N$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears as an open problem in the geodesics problem list compiled from the 2010 Tianjin workshop. Related Frankel-type questions for Finsler manifolds with positive flag curvature are known to be open (with counterexamples in the non-reversible case constructed by Bryant–Foulon–Ivanov–Matveev–Ziller), but no resolution of this specific 3-dimensional reversible intersection question was found.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and questions about geodesics
status_evidence.snippet: Question 8.5.4. Let (M^3,F) be a closed 3-dimensional reversible Finsler manifold of positive flag curvature and N be a closed totally geodesic 2-dimensional submanifold. Is it true that each closed geodesic intersects this submanifold or lies on it?
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open question in a problem list on geodesics.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic behavior for Finsler metrics of constant positive flag curvature on S^2
status_evidence.snippet: Example of a Finsler metric on S^2 with positive flag curvature such that no two closed geodesics intersect; not possible when reversible or of constant flag curvature.
status_evidence.claim: Related Frankel-type intersection questions for Finsler manifolds remain actively studied with the reversible case being more restrictive.
